text: Here's how memory normally works.
Your brain throws most of your life away.
What you ate last Tuesday. What your teacher wore. Gone.
And that's not a bug. It's cleaning.
You don't have that. Nothing ever drains.
Instead of a bucket... you have a palace.
Every day of your life is a door. And every door still opens.
This isn't pure fiction. A few dozen people on Earth have something close to it.
Give them any date, and they'll tell you what they did that day.
You have it turned all the way up.
Okay. I can't remember being a baby. So... not everything.
School? You read every book once. That's it. Forever.
Did you even study?!
I read it. In September.
Memory champions can memorize a whole shuffled deck of cards in under twenty seconds.
They use a trick that's two and a half thousand years old. The memory palace.
You do it in one glance.
Ace of spades, seven of hearts... how?!
I never said that!
Friday, June fourteenth, twelve oh two. You said, and I quote: I would never eat pineapple pizza.
You win every argument. Every single one.
People stop arguing with you. Then... they stop talking to you.
Five years later, on your twenty-first birthday, Sam drags you to Las Vegas.
Blackjack. Six decks. Three hundred and twelve cards. You remember every single one that's been played.
Wait... we're up how much?!
Congratulations. You're welcome to leave. And never come back.
Fair.
But that's the future. Right now, someone needs you.
Your grandma Ayla is your favorite person in the world.
She taught you to dance, to cook... and to cheat at cards.
Never measure the butter, Lina. The heart measures.
Then she starts forgetting things.
Her keys. Your mom's birthday. Whole afternoons.
Have you seen my keys, dear? I just had them.
It's Alzheimer's. It's early... but it will get worse.
You remember everything. And the person you love most is slowly forgetting everything.
And here's the price nobody talks about.
You can't forget the bad days either.
Every embarrassing moment. Every goodbye. In perfect detail. On repeat.
The most famous memory man in history wrote things on paper and burned them, hoping to forget. It didn't work.
Scientists think forgetting is actually healthy. It clears space, so you can move on.
There's an experimental treatment. It would let you forget... like everyone else.
No more replays. No more hurt. You'd be normal.
I'm sorry, dear... have we met?
It's the worst day. She doesn't know you.
But you know something about her that nobody else remembers.
Ten years ago, she hummed a song while she was cooking. Just once.
The song from her wedding.
Lina...? My Lina. You came.
For three minutes, she's back. She laughs. She tells you the butter story again.
Then... she's gone.
You'll keep every memory. The good ones, and the ones that hurt.
Because someone has to remember for her.
Then, one night, you notice something impossible.
One door in your palace is empty. Saturday, March fourteenth, six years ago. Not a single second.
I don't forget things. I can't.
So... who took it?
If you could never forget one day of your life, which day would it be? Tell us in the comments.
And if you'd have kept the memories too... subscribe. Part two is coming.
